summary: The agent successfully extracted structured data from pharmacy label images using OCR and created a formatted Excel output. This skill captures the reusable pattern of OCR-based data extraction from images, handling multiple date formats (EXP/MFG dates, MM/YYYY), multiple price formats (RM, $, MYR), and outputting to Excel with validation. Key lessons: use python3 not python, handle ambiguous month/day ordering via context clues, normalize partial dates to full dates, and verify Excel structure matches requirements.

The trace demonstrates successful OCR-based extraction from order images with duplicate detection against a known_orders.csv reference. The key reusable patterns are: (1) loading a validation CSV to filter/order extracted IDs, (2) first-occurrence deduplication with null values for duplicates, (3) date normalization to ISO format, (4) price formatting as strings with 2 decimal places, and (5) filename-sorted processing. The existing image-to-structured-excel skill needs extension for reference-based validation and deduplication workflows.

This trace reveals a new pattern: OCR-based extraction with CSV roster lookup and cross-referenced field enrichment. Key challenges were (1) date format ambiguity (DD/MM/YYYY vs MM/DD/YYYY) requiring sample inspection before parsing, (2) proper empty cell handling in Excel (empty strings vs None), and (3) partial roster matches where some extracted codes exist in reference data while others don't. The existing image-to-structured-excel skill covers basic OCR→Excel but lacks roster-based enrichment, multi-format date detection, and claim/invoice-specific patterns. Updating this skill is more appropriate than creating a duplicate.

The trace shows successful invoice extraction from images with key learnings: (1) multiple total keywords must be checked in priority order (GRAND TOTAL, TOTAL DUE, TOTAL), (2) date format detection is critical - the agent fixed a bug where 02/14/2024 was initially mis-parsed, (3) the existing image-to-structured-excel skill covers this well but needs invoice-specific patterns added. The skill should be updated with invoice-specific extraction patterns, better date format detection guidance, and the total keyword priority system discovered in this trace.

This utility bill extraction task revealed several reusable patterns not fully covered by the existing image-to-structured-excel skill: multi-format date auto-detection (DD/MM vs MM/DD with second-value > 12 rule), multi-line OCR amount extraction (handling split 'TOTAL\\n\\nDUE' patterns), multiple amount keyword fallbacks (PAY THIS AMOUNT, CURRENT CHARGES, AMOUNT DUE, TOTAL DUE), and template workbook preservation (keeping cover sheet intact while updating data sheet). These patterns generalize to any document OCR task with inconsistent formats.

The agent attempted OCR extraction from construction measurement forms but encountered issues with OCR artifacts corrupting unit symbols (e.g., 'm?' instead of 'm³') and initially extracted only 2 of 3 line items due to brittle parsing. The task ultimately failed verification. This skill captures the corrected extraction patterns, OCR normalization techniques, and multi-line item parsing strategies that were discovered through trial and error.

This trace reveals a fuel receipt extraction task that required filtering non-receipt images, handling date format auto-detection (MM/DD vs DD/YYYY), and dealing with OCR noise (zeros vs letter O in TXN REF). The agent succeeded but made a brittle initial assumption about date formats. The existing image-to-structured-excel skill already covers much of this but lacks specific patterns for fuel/transaction receipts and document type classification. I'll add a new fuel-receipt-extraction skill that captures the specific patterns and filtering logic, plus update the existing skill with document type classification guidance.

The trace reveals a case settlement extraction task where the agent had to: 1) Walk a nested directory structure (cases/case_*/{purchases,credits,admin}/), 2) Classify document types (purchase receipt vs credit note vs admin), 3) Handle fragmented OCR with split-line patterns like 'DIT NO:' instead of 'CREDIT NO:', 4) Parse dates with mixed formats (DD/MM/YYYY, MM/DD/YYYY, YYYY-MM-DD), 5) Deduplicate by document_ref within each case, 6) Aggregate to case-level summary with net_amount calculations. The agent succeeded but went through multiple debug cycles for OCR fragmentation issues. Key learning: credit note OCR has severe fragmentation ('CRE

CRE

DATE:

DIT NO:'), requiring multi-line regex or line-by-line scanning. Also learned: admin documents must be filtered by checking for absence of transaction keywords. This is distinct from fuel-receipt-extraction (which filters by TXN REF presence) and image-to-structured-excel (which handles reference files and templates). This task has no reference CSV, no template preservation, but has hierarchical aggregation and case-level deduplication.
